title: Dungeon Descent: Consumables Buy Depth
isolation: candidate runs as an isolated stdin->stdout subprocess via isorun; the reward horizon used only for score-cap normalization stays in the evaluator process, never sent to the candidate
strategies: reckless-descend (evaluator's own baseline): always descend, never grind/heal/ward -> dies early on most instances -> banked 0 -> normalizes to exactly 0.1

fixed HP-threshold reactive policy: grinds when HP% is low, wards only when its OWN current HP fraction looks risky -- ignorant of the actual upcoming hazard magnitude, so it strides into an unseen lethal spike at high HP and dies, forfeiting all banked reward, on 8/10 instances

inventory-conditioned depth policy (strong): scans the hazard curve, reserves wards specifically for hits that exceed max HP (unhealable by any amount of potions/grinding), heals proactively before healable-but-big hits, and stops/banks once its resources can no longer clear what's ahead -- survives all 10 instances and reaches far greater depth

richer planners that also weigh turn-budget efficiency, reorder which unhealable hits to tank vs. skip when wards are scarcer than spikes, or grind further ahead of a drought to bank even deeper safely
